scenario: [LGRA.2.9.7] `\'` in a double-quoted string is accepted and denotes an apostrophe, observed at run time on both runtimes at three sites. In a `where` literal: the rule matches the Item whose label is `it's` and not the control Item whose label keeps the backslash, so a literal lowered with its raw text fires on the wrong Item. In a `log` literal with no interpolation, the message is `it's`. In a literal piece beside an interpolation, the message is `a's`. PATH PINNED: `dsc.strlit.simple_escape`'s `\'` arm, reached through `lgra_2_9_4_decode` from each literal's lowering into the `.dsc`, then libds's and Mercury's evaluation of that literal and rendering of the log. Without the arm the program is refused with DS_PARSE_BAD_ESCAPE per [LGRA.2.9.4].
rules_ds:
schema Item scope logical:
    entity_id: String key
    label: String mutable

rule hit:
    Item i where i.label == "it\'s"
->
    log info "it\'s"
    log info "{i.entity_id}\'s"
